title: Bringing Science Full Circle: Ben Schooler Shares What Has Motivated His Path at BioMarin
summary: Ben Schooler’s career reflects a deep respect for science, connection and the patients BioMarin serves. Learn more about what inspires his work.
body_markdown:
## **CONNECTION**


What role does connection play at BioMarin?


Some of the most meaningful connections I’ve had at BioMarin have been with patients and their families. When I was leading lab operations, I had the chance to host facility tours for patients and their families. One family stands out to this day – they had two children living with CLN2 disease. The older sibling’s diagnosis prompted evaluation of the younger sibling, who was diagnosed approximately two years earlier in life. Seeing them together made the importance of early diagnosis tangible. It reinforced how meaningful it can be for families to have answers sooner and to better understand the path ahead. And it also made our work incredibly real.


I’ve been fortunate to meet several people on our therapies and hear directly how our medicines have changed their daily lives. Those moments have stayed with me and are a big reason I’ve chosen to spend much of my career here.


Connections inside BioMarin have mattered too. Moving from R&D into Technical Operations was a big leap for me. I knew the science, but manufacturing, quality and supply chain were completely new. I made the move because I wanted to understand another part of the business, and I was lucky to work with a leadership team that welcomed my curiosity. They didn’t expect me to have all the answers – they invested the time to teach me and challenge me. That experience shaped how I think about leadership and collaboration today.


More broadly, I’ve seen BioMarin’s Employee Resource Groups evolve from networks into meaningful, leadership-sponsored communities that help shape our culture. Catalysts for Change is a great example. It creates space for honest conversations about the issues affecting our lives, both inside and outside of work, and reminds us that connection, empathy and understanding are not soft skills – they’re essential to how we lead and collaborate together.
